# Package `thaumcraft.api`

[All packages](README.md)

The public Thaumcraft API of the 1.21.1 port.

The API keeps the original TC4 names and semantics; every Minecraft type is the native 1.21.1 one and every class is bound to the native implementation rather than to a copy of it.

Types: [`BlockCoordinates`](#blockcoordinates), [`IArchitect`](#iarchitect), [`IGoggles`](#igoggles), [`IRepairable`](#irepairable), [`IRepairableExtended`](#irepairableextended), [`IRunicArmor`](#irunicarmor), [`IScribeTools`](#iscribetools), [`IThaumcraftAddon`](#ithaumcraftaddon), [`IVisDiscountGear`](#ivisdiscountgear), [`IWarpingGear`](#iwarpinggear), [`ItemApi`](#itemapi), [`ItemRunic`](#itemrunic), [`OreDictionaryNames`](#oredictionarynames), [`ThaumcraftApi`](#thaumcraftapi), [`ThaumcraftApiHelper`](#thaumcraftapihelper), [`ThaumcraftFX`](#thaumcraftfx), [`ThaumcraftMaterials`](#thaumcraftmaterials), [`ThaumcraftSoundIds`](#thaumcraftsoundids), [`TileThaumcraft`](#tilethaumcraft), [`WorldCoordinates`](#worldcoordinates)

## BlockCoordinates

```java
public class BlockCoordinates implements Comparable<BlockCoordinates>
```

The original TC4 mutable block coordinate.

Original `thaumcraft/api/BlockCoordinates.java`: a public holder of three coordinates with `equals`, `hashCode`, `compareWorldCoordinate`, `set`, the two squared distances and the NBT helpers of the keys `b_x`, `b_y` and `b_z`. The class was the published value type of the architect preview of the original, so an add-on that highlights the blocks of an architect area needs it.

Forced 1.21.1 change: `TileEntity` became `BlockEntity` and `NBTTagCompound` became `CompoundTag`; the coordinates, the comparison, the hash and the NBT keys are the original ones. The native gameplay of the architect works on `BlockPos` and on the bounded `thaumcraft.common.items.wands.WandArchitect.Area`, so this class carries no native state: it is the published type of the original, nothing more.

## IArchitect

```java
public interface IArchitect
```

The Architect focus capability of the original TC4 API.

Original `thaumcraft/api/IArchitect.java:17-28` published three members: the list of the blocks the architect would touch (`ArrayList<BlockCoordinates> getArchitectBlocks(ItemStack, World, int, int, int, int, EntityPlayer)`), the axis the client has to draw (`boolean showAxis(ItemStack, World, EntityPlayer, int, EnumAxis)`) and its own `EnumAxis` of the three axes. The native architect is a server-authoritative re-implementation: the server owns the area of the focus (`WandArchitect.Area`), the client draws the area of the value the server sent and no block list of the preview travels at all. The published members are therefore the server side truth of the original: an add-on that asks a focus for the blocks of its area or for the axes of its preview gets the original answer, and the published value type of the original, `BlockCoordinates`, is the type of that list.

Forced 1.21.1 change: `World` became `Level` and `EntityPlayer` became `Player`; the two native architect foci publish the two members of the original with the original rules. The native `getMaxAreaSize(ItemStack)` and `getAxisModes()` are the additions of the port: the original had no member for the size of the area.

<a id="iarchitect-getarchitectblocks"></a>
```java
ArrayList<BlockCoordinates> getArchitectBlocks(ItemStack wand, Level world, int x, int y, int z, int side, Player player)
```

Original `IArchitect:18` - the blocks the architect would touch.

**Returns:** the blocks of the area, in the order of the original walk

**Parameters:**
- `wand` — the wand that holds the focus, as the original implementations read it
- `world` — the world of the area
- `x` — the X coordinate of the anchor
- `y` — the Y coordinate of the anchor
- `z` — the Z coordinate of the anchor
- `side` — the face of the anchor, the ordinal of the original direction
- `player` — the player that owns the preview

<a id="iarchitect-showaxis"></a>
```java
boolean showAxis(ItemStack wand, Level world, Player player, int side, EnumAxis axis)
```

Original `IArchitect:20` - the axis the client has to draw.

**Returns:** whether that axis is part of the preview

**Parameters:**
- `wand` — the wand that holds the focus, as the original implementations read it
- `world` — the world of the area
- `player` — the player that owns the preview
- `side` — the face of the anchor, the ordinal of the original direction
- `axis` — the axis of the preview


The size of the area of the focus, the addition of the port.

**Returns:** the maximum radius of the area

## IThaumcraftAddon

```java
public interface IThaumcraftAddon
```

The point where an add-on does its Thaumcraft registrations.

A 1.7.10 add-on declared `dependencies = "after:Thaumcraft"` and registered its aspects, object tags, recipes, research and wand parts in `init` or `postInit`, when every item of every mod and every Thaumcraft registry existed. The 1.21.1 loaders give no such order: on Fabric the `main` entrypoints of mods run in an unspecified order, so an add-on that looks up a Thaumcraft item from its own initializer can run before Thaumcraft registered it. Thaumcraft calls `onThaumcraftReady()` once, when it is safe:
- after every mod registered its items, blocks and entities, and after Thaumcraft registered its content, aspects, research, wand parts and recipes;
- on the main thread, before any world loads, on both physical sides (client and dedicated server), like the 1.7.10 init phases. Register on both sides: a client and its server must know the same research keys.

Registering the hook:
- **Fabric:** list the class under the `"thaumcraft"` entrypoint of `fabric.mod.json`: `"entrypoints": {"thaumcraft": ["com.example.MyAddon"]}`.
- **NeoForge:** annotate the class with `Addon`; it needs a public constructor without arguments. The hook runs from `FMLCommonSetupEvent`'s main-thread work queue.
- **Either loader:** call `ThaumcraftApi.whenReady(Runnable)` from your own initializer.

The order among add-ons is not specified. Items and blocks themselves are registered in your own initializer or registry events as usual; this hook is for the Thaumcraft registrations that refer to them.

<a id="ithaumcraftaddon-onthaumcraftready"></a>
```java
void onThaumcraftReady()
```

Registers the add-on's Thaumcraft content. Called exactly once per game instance.

### Addon

```java
@interface Addon
```

Marks an `IThaumcraftAddon` for discovery on NeoForge. Fabric uses the `"thaumcraft"` entrypoint instead.

## IWarpingGear

```java
public interface IWarpingGear
```

Original thaumcraft.api.IWarpingGear: an item that adds warp to whoever holds or wears it, for as long as it is held or worn.

Original WarpEvents.getWarpFromGear: the item in the main hand, the four armor pieces and the four accessory slots (Baubles in 1.7.10) are counted; the off hand and the rest of the inventory are not. Void metal tools and armor each add one. The sum takes part in the warp events like the permanent and sticky warp of the player's knowledge.

```java
int getWarp(ItemStack stack, Player player)
```

## ItemApi

```java
public class ItemApi
```

The original TC4 reflective item/block lookup.

Forced 1.21.1 change: the original reflected over `thaumcraft.common.config.ConfigItems` and `ConfigBlocks`. The native port has no such classes and 1.21.1 has no metadata, so an original field name and metadata (`getItem("itemResource", 2)`) are resolved through the table `data/thaumcraft/tc4/legacy_ids.json` (written by `scripts/porting/extract_legacy_ids.py`, reference `docs/api/LEGACY_IDS.md`). Any other name is resolved through the live registries (a plain name means `thaumcraft:<name>`) and only then through the original reflective field names for an add-on that still publishes them.

The table is read from the classpath on the first legacy lookup and never needs a running game; the native objects are taken from the registries at the time of each call.

<a id="itemapi-wildcard"></a>
```java
public static final int WILDCARD
```

`OreDictionary.WILDCARD_VALUE`: every metadata of an original field.

<a id="itemapi-getitem"></a>
```java
public static ItemStack getItem(String itemString, int meta)
```

Returns a fresh named stack, or null for null/empty/malformed/missing names (failed lookups log). An original `ConfigItems` field name selects its 1.21.1 item by the original metadata; a field with a single item keeps the metadata as the wear of a damageable stack, as the original did. Any other name is a namespaced item id, where the metadata only applies wear to a damageable stack.

<a id="itemapi-getblock"></a>
```java
public static ItemStack getBlock(String itemString, int meta)
```

Returns a fresh named block-item stack, or null for null/empty/malformed/missing names (failed lookups log). An original `ConfigBlocks` field name selects the item form of the original metadata; when the metadata selects a state that the block's own item places, the stack carries it as `minecraft:block_state`. Any other name is a namespaced block id.

The 1.21.1 item id of an original field and metadata: the item of a `ConfigItems` field, the item form of a `ConfigBlocks` field. Null for an unknown name or metadata, for a variant with no 1.21.1 counterpart and for the wildcard of a field with several items (`legacyItemIds`).


Every 1.21.1 item id an original field and metadata stands for: one id, or for `WILDCARD` every distinct item of the field, in metadata order. Empty for an unknown name.

## OreDictionaryNames

```java
public final class OreDictionaryNames
```

The 1.7.10 Forge ore dictionary names an add-on used, as 1.21.1 item tags.

1.21.1 has no ore dictionary; item tags took its place, and the shared `c:` tags of Fabric and NeoForge hold the materials of every mod. The recipe and object tag API accepts the old names and resolves them here, so `ThaumcraftApi.registerObjectTag("ingotCopper", aspects)` and a recipe ingredient `"ingotCopper"` keep working. The first rule that applies wins:
- the ore names Thaumcraft 4 itself registered or used (`nuggetThaumium`, `shardAir`, `logWood`, `stickWood`, `ingotIron`...) are the `thaumcraft:original_ore/*` tags, which hold the Thaumcraft items and the vanilla ones the name held in 1.7.10;
- a namespaced id (`"c:ingots/copper"`, `"minecraft:logs"`) is that tag;
- a Forge name of a vanilla thing (`blockGlass`, `slimeball`, `dyeRed`...) is its conventional tag;
- a name of the Forge convention `<kind><Material>` is `c:<kinds>/<material>`: `ingotCopper` is `c:ingots/copper`, `oreLapis` `c:ores/lapis`, `blockSilver` `c:storage_blocks/silver`, `dustRedstone` `c:dusts/redstone`, `gemNetherQuartz` `c:gems/nether_quartz`.

Any other name answers null. A tag only names its members; which items it holds is decided by the data packs of the game, and a material no mod adds has an empty tag, exactly like an empty ore dictionary entry of 1.7.10.

<a id="oredictionarynames-itemtag"></a>
```java
public static TagKey<Item> itemTag(String name)
```

The item tag of an ore dictionary name or a namespaced tag id; null when no rule applies.

<a id="oredictionarynames-tagid"></a>
```java
public static ResourceLocation tagId(String name)
```

The tag id of an ore dictionary name or a namespaced tag id; null when no rule applies.

## ThaumcraftApi

```java
public final class ThaumcraftApi
```

The public registration facade of the native port.

It publishes the original scan/object-tag registries, the original materials, the original recipe, smelting-bonus and warp registries and the original plug point between the API and the gameplay internals. Every answer is read from the native implementation; nothing is copied.

<a id="thaumcraftapi-armormatspecial"></a>
```java
public static ArmorMaterial armorMatSpecial()
```

Original `armorMatSpecial` (oracle `thaumcraft/api/ThaumcraftApi.java:52`): durability 25, the defenses 1/3/2/1 and the enchantability 25. The original published it as a field; the native answers through an accessor with a plain `ArmorMaterial` object holding the original numbers (the iron equip sound, no repair ingredient, no worn layer). It is **not in the armour material registry** and has no holder or key: wrap it with `Holder.direct` to build an item from it, or register a material of your own. The registered `thaumcraft:special` is a different object, the adapter of the goggles (gold repair, the goggles' worn layer), not this one. See `ThaumcraftMaterials`.

<a id="thaumcraftapi-armormatvoidfortress"></a>
```java
public static ArmorMaterial armorMatVoidFortress()
```

Original `armorMatVoidFortress` (oracle `thaumcraft/api/ThaumcraftApi.java:55`): durability 18, the defenses 4/8/7/4 and the enchantability 10. The original published it as a field; the native answers through an accessor with a plain `ArmorMaterial` object holding the original defences. It is **not in the armour material registry** and has no holder or key: wrap it with `Holder.direct` to build an item from it, or register a material of your own. See `ThaumcraftMaterials`.

Forced 1.21.1 change: the original stores `new ItemStack(out.getItem(), 0, out.getItemDamage())` (oracle `thaumcraft/api/ThaumcraftApi.java:80-82`), so the registry amount is always zero: the arcane furnace decides how many units it pays with its own bellows rolls (oracle `thaumcraft/common/tiles/TileArcaneFurnace.java:237-259`). 1.21.1 cannot hold an amount-zero stack as a real stack, because `ItemStack.copy()` of an amount-zero stack returns the shared `ItemStack.EMPTY` and the entry would lose its item. The native registry therefore keeps the amount the addon registered; the furnace still ignores it and pays its own amount.

<a id="thaumcraftapi-ismirrorsallowed"></a>
```java
public static boolean isMirrorsAllowed()
```

The original `Config.allowMirrors`: may the player build and use the mirrors? Not a 1.7.10 method: an add-on of the original read the public field `thaumcraft.common.config.Config.allowMirrors` (and, on a client, its synced copy `CallowMirrors`).

**What it means.** Thaumcraft's own switch (config key `allow_mirrors`, default `true`). While it is off, the research of the Magic Mirror, the Essentia Mirror and the Hand Mirror (keys `MIRROR`, `MIRRORESSENTIA`, `MIRRORHAND`) is disabled, so nobody can learn it. An add-on feature that is built on a mirror (a focus that needs one as an ingredient, say) should follow the same switch. The mod does not enforce the switch when a mirror is placed or used, and it removes no mirror that exists.

**Side and thread.** Either side. On the client thread it is the value the connected server sent when the player joined (the local configuration when not connected); on every other thread it is this installation's own server value, read from the configuration file at startup. It cannot change while a world runs (restart scoped). Cheap and allocation free; safe to call every tick.

<a id="thaumcraftapi-iswardedstoneallowed"></a>
```java
public static boolean isWardedStoneAllowed()
```

The original `Config.wardedStone`: do warded stone, warded glass, arcane doors and arcane pressure plates belong to their owner? Not a 1.7.10 method: an add-on of the original read the public field `thaumcraft.common.config.Config.wardedStone` (client copy `CwardedStone`).

**What it means.** Thaumcraft's own switch (config key `allow_warded_stone`, default `true`). While it is on, warded doors, warded glass and warded pressure plates are unbreakable by mining (for everybody) and only the owner can take a warded block back with a wand; while it is off they have an ordinary hardness and anybody can remove them with a wand. It also gates the research of the warding focus and of the warded arcana (`FOCUSWARDING`, `WARDEDARCANA`), so an add-on block that builds on warded stone (a ward slab, a warding fence) should be offered only while it is on.

**Side and thread.** Same as `isMirrorsAllowed()`.

<a id="thaumcraftapi-registerobjecttag-5"></a>
```java

```

Registers the aspects of every member of an item tag; null aspects become empty, null tags are not guarded.

The members a tag has now are registered at once, like the 1.7.10 ore dictionary call. Tags are data: at mod initialization, when an add-on of 1.7.10 made this call, no tag is bound yet. The registration is therefore kept and applied again when a world starts (and on a client joining a server), and then it fills every member that has no registration of its own: a registration of the item itself wins over a tag, and a later tag registration wins over an earlier one.

## ThaumcraftApiHelper

```java
public class ThaumcraftApiHelper
```

The original TC4 static helper surface.

Forced 1.21.1 changes: `World`/`IBlockAccess`/`EntityPlayer`/`ItemStack` became `Level`/`BlockGetter`/`Player`/`ItemStack`, `ForgeDirection` became `Direction`, `MovingObjectPosition` became `BlockHitResult` and the Forge item NBT tag comparison became the native data-component comparison.

<a id="thaumcraftapihelper-culltags"></a>
```java
public static AspectList cullTags(AspectList temp)
```

Original cap of six aspects, dropping the least valuable ones first.

Forced 1.21.1 change (documented deviation from the original): the original started the search of the cheapest aspect at `Short.MAX_VALUE` and removed the cheapest one until six aspects were left (oracle `thaumcraft/api/ThaumcraftApiHelper.java:38-70`). When every weighted amount of the list was at least `Short.MAX_VALUE`, the original found no candidate, removed `null` - which changes nothing - and looped forever. The native port stops the culling when there is nothing left to drop, so the call always terminates; the result of a normal list is the original one, aspect for aspect.

<a id="thaumcraftapihelper-areitemsequal"></a>
```java
public static boolean areItemsEqual(ItemStack s1, ItemStack s2)
```

The original stack comparison.

Original `thaumcraft/api/ThaumcraftApiHelper.java:68-74`: two damageable stacks are the same item whatever their wear is, every other pair is the same item with the same damage value. The count of a stack is never part of the comparison.

Forced 1.21.1 change: `ItemStack.isItemStackDamageable()` became `ItemStack.isDamageableItem()`. Null and EMPTY are equivalent; exactly one absent stack returns false, and components are ignored rather than validated.


Original `thaumcraft/api/ThaumcraftApiHelper.java:95-97` and the oracle `thaumcraft/common/tiles/TileMagicWorkbench.java` read the cell `row + column * 3` of the grid, with the ROW as the first argument: the original recipes call `getStackInRowAndColumn(inv, 1, 0)` for the first cap of the sceptre, which is the slot 1 of the grid (oracle `thaumcraft/common/lib/crafting/ArcaneSceptreRecipe.java:42-46`).


Delegates the aspect-unit lookup, replacing a null result with a new empty list; does not convert to centivis. The installed handler returns a copy and treats null/empty input as empty; replacing internalMethods can change ownership/side effects.

<a id="thaumcraftapihelper-getobjectaspects-2"></a>
```java
public static AspectList getObjectAspects(ItemStack is, Level level)
```

Native world-scoped form: the level-free variant cannot resolve recipe-derived tags.

<a id="thaumcraftapihelper-getbonusobjecttags"></a>
```java
public static AspectList getBonusObjectTags(ItemStack is, AspectList ot)
```

The 1.7.10 signature, which cannot be answered without a world: the installed handler only returns a copy of `ot` (null becomes an empty list) and ignores `is`. The 1.7.10 enrichment of the base aspects with the contents of a container and the bonuses of equipment and enchantments is *not* done here: use `getBonusObjectTags(ItemStack, AspectList, Level)` (or `getObjectAspects(ItemStack, Level)`, which already holds all of it). Its contract differs, so do not just add the level to an old call.

<a id="thaumcraftapihelper-getbonusobjecttags-2"></a>
```java
public static AspectList getBonusObjectTags(ItemStack is, AspectList bonus, Level level)
```

The aspects of one item as `getObjectAspects(ItemStack, Level)` gives them, plus `bonus` on top: the world-scoped form of the original `getBonusObjectTags(ItemStack, AspectList)`. Not a 1.7.10 signature.

**This is not the 1.7.10 contract.** The original took the BASE aspects of the item in its second argument and returned them enriched with the bonuses. Here the base is already part of the result, so do not pass `getObjectAspects(stack, level)` as `bonus`: every amount would be counted twice. Pass `null` for the aspects of the stack alone, or only the extra aspects you want added.

**The result** is a new list, per single item (the count of the stack is not applied). Its base part is *exactly* `getObjectAspects(stack, level)`, which is already the complete answer of a scan: the registered, recipe-derived or inferred aspects of the item (a group of damage values registered together is resolved as a scan resolves it), the contents of an essentia container (a filled jar, a phial, a crystal, wisp essence, a bound jar label), and the bonuses of worn equipment and of enchantments, culled to the six most valuable aspects (`cullTags`) without capping amounts. This method adds only `bonus`, by summing, *after* the culling, so the result can hold more than six aspects. `bonus` is never modified. When you have no bonus to add, `getObjectAspects(stack, level)` is the plain way to ask.

An empty or null stack or a null level contributes nothing: the result is then a copy of `bonus` (an empty list for null). A replaced handler that answers null gives an empty list. Either side; the recipe-derived aspects are read from the recipes of `level`.


Delegates to the installed handler and normalizes null results to an empty list; meta is native damage points. Unlike 1.7.10 recipe derivation, the installed level-free handler only reads catalogue/registered aspect units (null item becomes empty). Use getObjectAspects(ItemStack, Level) for 1.21.1 scan-complete results; no level-aware generate facade is implemented here.

<a id="thaumcraftapihelper-hasscanneditem"></a>
```java
public static boolean hasScannedItem(Player player, ItemStack stack)
```

Whether the player has scanned the item of the stack with a thaumometer: the answer the thaumometer readout uses to show the aspects of a target that was already scanned. Not a 1.7.10 member (the original compared a hash of the item and its metadata in `Thaumcraft.proxy.getScannedObjects`).

**Identity.** The item is looked up by its registry id (the marker `"@" + id`, as `ItemThaumometer` writes it for the item it picked from a block or an item entity); the count, the damage and the data components of the stack do not matter, and there is no metadata in 1.21.1. The marker of an advanced scan (`"#" + id`) counts as scanned too. Scanning a dropped item counts for that item and scanning a block for the item a pick-block of it gives (a redstone wire is `minecraft:redstone`); scanning a mob counts for no item.

False for a null player, a null or empty stack, and an item nobody scanned. Works on both sides for the client's own player (its knowledge is synced); the knowledge of another player is only known to the server.

<a id="thaumcraftapihelper-discoveraspect"></a>
```java
public static boolean discoverAspect(ServerPlayer player, Aspect aspect)
```

Marks the aspect as discovered for the player, so the research table and the thaumometer treat it as known, and syncs the player's knowledge to the client. The native counterpart of the original `PlayerKnowledge.addDiscoveredAspect`. Not a 1.7.10 helper member.

The aspect starts with an empty research pool; an aspect the player already knows keeps its pool. It does *not* check that the parents of a compound aspect are known (a scan does), shows no discovery notice and gives no research points: it is the quiet "learn this aspect" of the original, for an item that copies knowledge. (A positive `addAspectPool` discovers the aspect too, because in the player's knowledge an aspect is discovered exactly when it has a pool entry.) Only a registered aspect can be discovered.

Server side only, on the server thread (another thread throws `IllegalStateException`).

**Returns:** true when this call discovered the aspect; false when the player already knew it, on a client, for a null player or aspect, for an aspect that is not registered under its tag, and when the player's knowledge could not be read (it is kept untouched then, as everywhere else)

<a id="thaumcraftapihelper-getscans"></a>
```java
public static Scans getScans(Player player)
```

The scan markers of the player: everything the thaumometer recorded for items (and the blocks they were picked from), entities and phenomena (aura nodes). An immutable snapshot, so a Tome of Sharing can copy what one player scanned to another with `addScans`.

**The markers are the mod's own keys** and are meant to travel unchanged, not to be built or parsed: a basic scan is `"@"` followed by the registry id of the item or the name of the entity or phenomenon, an advanced scan `"#"` followed by the same (it replaces the `"@"` marker). A marker is never empty and at most 1024 characters long (`Scans.MAX_KEY_LENGTH`): a longer one in the knowledge (the mod never writes one; a hand-edited save or an add-on's own scan handler could) is left out of the snapshot instead of failing the call.

**Not included:** the research clues a scan revealed (`"@KEY"` entries among the completed research; `getCompletedResearch` leaves them out and `completeResearch` refuses them), the discovered aspects (`getDiscoveredAspects(Player)`) and the research points (`getAspectPool`).

Both sides for the client's own player; the knowledge of another player is only known to the server. An empty snapshot for a null player and for knowledge that could not be read. Never throws for the content of the knowledge.

<a id="thaumcraftapihelper-addscans"></a>
```java
public static int addScans(ServerPlayer player, Scans scans)
```

Adds scan markers to the player's knowledge and syncs it to the client: the native counterpart of the original `ResearchManager.completeScannedObject/Entity/Phenomena`. Not a 1.7.10 helper member. The markers are those of `getScans`; they give no research points, aspects or clues, only the fact "scanned".

A marker the player already has is not added again, in either of its two forms: a basic marker (`"@x"`) is skipped when the player holds `"@x"` or `"#x"`; an advanced marker (`"#x"`) is added and replaces a basic one. Adding is idempotent. The resulting knowledge and the returned count do not depend on the order of the markers: a snapshot that holds both `"@x"` and `"#x"` (an add-on can build one by hand) counts as the one marker `"#x"`.

Server side only, on the server thread (another thread throws `IllegalStateException`).

**Returns:** the number of markers that were new; the player is synced only when it is above zero. Zero on a client, for null arguments and when the player's knowledge could not be read (nothing is changed then)

<a id="thaumcraftapihelper-iswoodlog"></a>
```java
public static boolean isWoodLog(Level level, BlockPos pos)
```

Whether the block at the position is a log: the 1.21.1 form of the original `Utils.isWoodLog(world, x, y, z)`. It answers "may the furthest-log walk of `breakFurthestBlock` step on this cell", and nothing else: it says nothing about whether the block belongs to a tree.

**The rule.** True for a block in the block tag `#minecraft:logs`: every log, wood, stripped log and stem of the tag, the plain oak log among them, and the Greatwood and Silverwood logs of Thaumcraft. False for everything else: leaf blocks, planks, air, and a log of another mod that is not in the tag. The original accepted every non-air block that can sustain leaves (a log does, a leaf block does not) and every entry of its list of ore dictionary logs; in 1.21.1 the tag is both (original `Utils.java:202-211`, read in `docs/analysis/2026-10-19-golem-lumber.md`). It is the broad original rule, not the set of the port's own Axe of the Stream, which deliberately fells a narrower one (the unstripped logs of the six old trees and the Greatwood and Silverwood logs).

Only the block state is read (no block entity, no hardness, no ownership). A position in a chunk that is not loaded, or outside the build height, is not a log; the call never loads a chunk. Either side; read-only; cheap. False for null arguments.

<a id="thaumcraftapihelper-findfurthestblock"></a>
```java
public static BlockPos findFurthestBlock(Level level, BlockPos pos, Block block)
```

Where `breakFurthestBlock` would break a block, without breaking anything: the end of the greedy walk that starts at the clicked log. Not a 1.7.10 method; it exists so that a caller can ask a claims or protection mod about the cell that will be broken, which can lie up to 24 blocks sideways and 48 up or down from `pos` (see the walk described at `breakFurthestBlock`).

The answer is the cell the next `breakFurthestBlock(level, pos, block, player)` call breaks, as long as no block changes in between and the player is allowed to break it; it is `pos` itself when no other log qualifies. It is a new immutable position. Felling a tree with protection is therefore a loop of: find the cell, ask your protection about that cell, call `breakFurthestBlock` only if it agrees (and stop the loop when it does not).

Null when nothing would be broken: a null argument, a `pos` outside the build height or in a chunk that is not loaded, a start that is not exactly `block` or is not a log (`isWoodLog`), and a start that cannot be broken. Read-only, loads no chunk (a cell in an unloaded chunk is no link of the walk), and keeps no state, so it works on either side and on any thread that may read the level.

**Parameters:**
- `level` — the level
- `pos` — the clicked log, where the walk starts
- `block` — the block the walk follows, normally `level.getBlockState(pos).getBlock()`

<a id="thaumcraftapihelper-breakfurthestblock"></a>
```java
public static boolean breakFurthestBlock(Level level, BlockPos pos, Block block, Player player)
```

Breaks the log at the far end of a tree, as the original Axe of the Stream did when it felled a tree from the clicked log: the 1.21.1 form of the original `BlockUtils.breakFurthestBlock(world, x, y, z, block, player)`. One call breaks ONE block; felling a whole tree is a loop of the caller.

**What "furthest" means.** A greedy walk, not a search of the whole tree. It starts at `pos` with a distance of zero. At each step it scans the cells within two blocks of the cell it stands on, in the order x from -2 to +2, y from +2 down to -2, z from -2 to +2, and moves to the FIRST cell that (1) holds exactly `block` (the same block, not the same tag; the log axis and other state properties are not compared), (2) satisfies `isWoodLog`, (3) can be broken (a destroy speed of zero or more) and (4) is strictly further from `pos` than the cell the walk reached before (squared distance, so an equal distance does not count). Then it repeats from there and stops when no cell qualifies. Consequences: gaps of up to two blocks and diagonals are crossed; a branch that is scanned first and ends early hides a longer branch (the walk is the first local maximum, not the farthest log of the tree); a neighbouring tree of the same wood is followed too. The walk never leaves the box |dx| &lt;= 24, |dy| &lt;= 48, |dz| &lt;= 24 around `pos`; the first scanned cell outside the box ends the whole walk (an original quirk: the remaining cells of that scan are not looked at). `findFurthestBlock` answers where it ends without breaking anything.

**What is broken.** Only the cell the walk ended on; the logs on the way stay. The start must itself be a log of `block`: for any other start (air, dirt, a chest...) nothing is broken and the answer is false. (The original broke the start whatever it was, because its axe called `isWoodLog` first; as a public helper this one asks that itself, so a position forwarded by a client cannot be used to mine an arbitrary block.) When no other log qualifies, the start itself is the cell that is broken.

**Drops.** The block is removed and drops its normal loot, rolled with the main-hand item of `player` (Fortune and Silk Touch count), as items at the broken cell; they do not follow the player. A creative player and a null player get no drops. The game rule for block drops applies.

**Tool wear: none.** The held item takes no damage, the player gets no statistics or exhaustion, and no loader break event is fired; the player's own Axe of the Stream does not use this helper in the port (it breaks through the normal break path and wears the axe).

**Protection.** The broken cell is far from `pos` and unknown before the call, so the game's own rules are applied to *that* cell: it must be inside the world border, and for a non-null player it must not be under spawn protection (`level.mayInteract(player, cell)`), and the player's game mode must allow breaking it (a spectator, and an adventure player without a tool that may break it, break nothing). When a rule refuses, the answer is false and nothing is changed. A claims, land-protection or permission mod is **not** asked, and no loader break event is fired, for any cell (the original asked nothing either): on claimed land call `findFurthestBlock` first, ask that mod about the cell it returns, and only then call this method. Do not check only the clicked `pos`: it is not the cell that is broken.

**Afterwards** every loaded cell within three blocks of the broken one gets a scheduled block tick 150 to 299 ticks later (the original's delayed neighbourhood update, which the leaves around a felled log answer) and clients see the block update.

**Return value.** True when the walk ended on a cell that is not air and can be broken, and the rules above agreed: that cell was handed to the harvester (like the original, true does not prove the block was removed: another mod can veto the removal and the call still answers true). False, with nothing changed, for a client level, a null argument, a start that is not a log of `block`, a start in a chunk that is not loaded, an end that a protection rule refuses and an end that cannot be broken. So `while (breakFurthestBlock(...))` ends once the start cell is air; put a limit on the loop anyway.

**Side and thread.** Server side, on the server thread; on another thread it throws `IllegalStateException`, because it breaks blocks and spawns items. It reads only loaded chunks and loads none: a cell in an unloaded chunk is no link of the walk (the original read, and so generated, such a chunk). Unlike the original it keeps no static state, so it is reentrant.

**Parameters:**
- `level` — the level; a client level returns false
- `pos` — the clicked log, where the walk starts
- `block` — the block the walk follows, normally `level.getBlockState(pos).getBlock()`
- `player` — the player who breaks it; decides the drops and the rules above; may be null

<a id="thaumcraftapihelper-raytraceignoringsource"></a>
```java
public static BlockHitResult rayTraceIgnoringSource(Level world, Vec3 v1, Vec3 v2, boolean includeFluid, boolean requireCollision, boolean reportMiss)
```

Original TC4 voxel ray that ignores the cell the ray starts in.

Forced 1.21.1 change: the result is a native `BlockHitResult`; the traversal itself is the native one, so the original per-face step quirks are replaced by the native block outline.

Endpoints are world coordinates in blocks; null world/endpoints or NaN components return null. The 1.7.10 includeFluid/reportMiss switches do not restore their old semantics: traversal tests block shapes only, never fluid shapes, and an unobstructed ray returns null even when reportMiss is true. Use Level.clip with a suitable ClipContext for 1.21.1 fluid/miss semantics. This method reads the world without explicitly mutating it.

### Scans

```java
public record Scans(Set<String> items, Set<String> entities, Set<String> phenomena)
```

An immutable snapshot of the scan markers of a player, as `getScans` returns it and `addScans` takes it. Not a 1.7.10 type. The three sets keep the order of the player's knowledge; each marker is a non-empty string of at most 1024 characters, `MAX_KEY_LENGTH` (the keys of the mod are far shorter; the bound keeps the knowledge sync packet well inside the limit of an NBT string). The constructor throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a marker that is null, empty or longer, and `NullPointerException` for a null set.

**Parameters:**
- `items` — markers of scanned items, for example `"@minecraft:diamond"`
- `entities` — markers of scanned entities
- `phenomena` — markers of scanned phenomena (aura nodes)

<a id="scans-max_key_length"></a>
```java
public static final int MAX_KEY_LENGTH
```

The longest marker a snapshot accepts, 1024 characters; the markers the mod writes are a registry id or a node id, well below it.

<a id="scans-empty"></a>
```java
public static final Scans EMPTY
```

No scan at all.

<a id="scans-scans"></a>
```java
public Scans(Set<String> items, Set<String> entities, Set<String> phenomena)
```

Copies the sets (insertion order kept) into unmodifiable ones; null sets, null or empty markers and markers longer than `MAX_KEY_LENGTH` are rejected with a `NullPointerException` or an `IllegalArgumentException`.

<a id="scans-isempty"></a>
```java
public boolean isEmpty()
```

True when no marker of any kind is held.

<a id="scans-size"></a>
```java
public int size()
```

The number of markers of all three kinds.

## ThaumcraftFX

```java
public final class ThaumcraftFX
```

The visual effects a 1.7.10 add-on sent to the players around a block with Thaumcraft's own packets.

Not a 1.7.10 class: an add-on of 1.7.10 built `thaumcraft.common.lib.network.fx.PacketFX*` itself and sent it with `PacketHandler.INSTANCE.sendToAllAround(..., 32)`. `blockSparkle`, `blockArc`, `zap`, `bubbles`, `essentiaTrail` and `visDrain` are those packets, with the original look. `sparkle`, `burst`, `blockRunes` and `smokeSpiral` are not: the 1.7.10 proxy drew them on the client only, so they are new senders, the server twins of the matching methods of `thaumcraft.api.client.ThaumcraftClientFX`, with no original packet. All of them reach the players within 32 blocks. Call them on the server thread of the level; on another thread they throw `IllegalStateException`. Colours are 0xRRGGBB.

<a id="thaumcraftfx-random_grey"></a>
```java
public static final int RANDOM_GREY
```

The original random grey of `blockSparkle`.

<a id="thaumcraftfx-blocksparkle"></a>
```java
public static void blockSparkle(ServerLevel level, BlockPos pos, int rgb)
```

Original `PacketFXBlockSparkle`: a burst of sparkles over a block; `RANDOM_GREY` for the grey of the original.

<a id="thaumcraftfx-blockarc"></a>
```java
public static void blockArc(ServerLevel level, Entity source, BlockPos target)
```

Original `PacketFXBlockArc`: an arc of lightning from an entity to a block.

<a id="thaumcraftfx-zap"></a>
```java
public static void zap(ServerLevel level, Vec3 from, Vec3 to)
```

Original `PacketFXBlockZap`: the bolt of a node between two points.

<a id="thaumcraftfx-bubbles"></a>
```java
public static void bubbles(ServerLevel level, BlockPos pos, int rgb)
```

Original `PacketFXBlockBubble`: the bubbles of a crucible around a block.

<a id="thaumcraftfx-essentiatrail"></a>
```java
public static void essentiaTrail(ServerLevel level, BlockPos consumer, BlockPos source, Aspect aspect)
```

Original `PacketFXEssentiaSource`: essentia flowing from `source` to the block that drew it.

<a id="thaumcraftfx-sparkle"></a>
```java
public static void sparkle(ServerLevel level, double x, double y, double z, float size, int type, float gravity)
```

The server twin of `ThaumcraftClientFX.sparkle`: every player within 32 blocks of the point is sent the sparkle and draws it with their own particle setting (so the sparkle is drawn with the chance of that call, not always). Not a packet of the original: the 1.7.10 proxy drew sparkles on the client only, and an add-on whose logic runs on the server had to send its own.

**Throws:** `IllegalArgumentException` — for the ranges of the client method

**Throws:** `IllegalStateException` — when not called on the server thread of the level

**Parameters:**
- `type` — 0 to 7, see the client method

<a id="thaumcraftfx-burst"></a>
```java
public static void burst(ServerLevel level, double x, double y, double z, float size)
```

The server twin of `thaumcraft.api.client.ThaumcraftClientFX.burst`: the white puff of the wisp, drawn by every player within 32 blocks of the point.

**Throws:** `IllegalArgumentException` — for the ranges of the client method

**Throws:** `IllegalStateException` — when not called on the server thread of the level

<a id="thaumcraftfx-blockrunes"></a>
```java
public static void blockRunes(ServerLevel level, double x, double y, double z, float red, float green, float blue, int duration, float gravity)
```

The server twin of `thaumcraft.api.client.ThaumcraftClientFX.blockRunes`: one rune glyph, drawn by every player within 32 blocks of the point. As in the client method, the position is the corner of a block and the rune appears half a block above and beside it on every axis.

**Throws:** `IllegalArgumentException` — for the ranges of the client method

**Throws:** `IllegalStateException` — when not called on the server thread of the level

<a id="thaumcraftfx-smokespiral"></a>
```java
public static void smokeSpiral(ServerLevel level, double x, double y, double z, float radius, int start, int minY, int rgb)
```

The server twin of `thaumcraft.api.client.ThaumcraftClientFX.smokeSpiral`: **one** puff of smoke that travels along a spiral, drawn by every player within 32 blocks of the point. One call is one puff, not a ring; the originals make the ring by calling it 5 to 33 times with random `start` angles, and so does a server caller that wants one.

**Throws:** `IllegalArgumentException` — for the ranges of the client method

**Throws:** `IllegalStateException` — when not called on the server thread of the level

<a id="thaumcraftfx-visdrain"></a>
```java
public static void visDrain(ServerLevel level, BlockPos consumer, BlockPos node, Aspect aspect)
```

Original `PacketFXVisDrain`: vis drawn from a node to the block that consumed it.

## ThaumcraftMaterials

```java
public final class ThaumcraftMaterials
```

The original TC4 material constants.

Forced 1.21.1 changes: `Item.ToolMaterial` became `Tier` and `ItemArmor.ArmorMaterial` became the registry-backed `ArmorMaterial`. The original numbers are preserved exactly: thaumium 3/400/7.0/2.0/22 with 2/6/5/2 armour and enchantability 25, void 4/150/8.0/3.0/10 with 3/7/6/3 and enchantability 10, fortress 40 durability with 3/7/6/3 and enchantability 25, the special armour 1/3/2/1 with enchantability 25 and the void fortress armour 4/8/7/4 with enchantability 10.

**Which materials have a registry key.** 1.21.1 armour items take a `Holder<ArmorMaterial>`, not the material object the 1.7.10 `ItemArmor` constructor took. Four materials are registered under the `thaumcraft` namespace for the armour families of the original: `thaumium` (`armorMatThaumiumHolder()`), `fortress` (`armorMatThaumiumFortressHolder()`), `void` (`armorMatVoidHolder()`) and `void_robe` (`armorMatVoidRobeHolder()`, the void numbers under another worn model). Each holder is the registry reference of its `ARMORMAT_*_KEY`, so `holder.value()` is the very object `armorMatThaumium()` and its siblings return. `ARMORMAT_SPECIAL` and `ARMORMAT_VOID_FORTRESS` are plain objects with the original numbers that are not in the registry at all, and have no key or holder: to build an item from one, wrap it with `Holder.direct`, or register a material of your own with your own worn textures, which is what an add-on whose armour looks different from Thaumcraft's does. A material named `thaumcraft:special` *is* registered, but it is the adapter of the goggles (the same defences and enchantability, a gold repair ingredient and the goggles' worn layer), a different object from `ARMORMAT_SPECIAL`, and is not part of this API.

```java
public static final Tier TOOLMAT_THAUMIUM
public static final Tier TOOLMAT_VOID
public static final Tier TOOLMAT_ELEMENTAL
```

```java
public static final ArmorMaterial ARMORMAT_SPECIAL
```

Original armorMatSpecial: 1/3/2/1, enchantability 25.


Oracle `thaumcraft/api/ThaumcraftApi.java:55`: `EnumHelper.addArmorMaterial("VOIDFORTRESS", 18, new int[]{4, 8, 7, 4}, 10)`. The enchantability of 1.7.10 lives on the item in 1.21.1 and has no place in the material.

## ThaumcraftSoundIds

```java
public final class ThaumcraftSoundIds
```

The ids of the sounds Thaumcraft registers, so an add-on that plays "its own" wand, zap or wind sound does not write the strings.

1.7.10 add-ons played them by name, `"thaumcraft:wand"`, `"thaumcraft:zap"`, `"thaumcraft:wind"`..., in `World.playSoundAtEntity`. In 1.21.1 each of them is a registered `SoundEvent` with the same path, declared in the mod's `sounds.json`. There is one constant for every sound event Thaumcraft registers, in the order it registers them, named after the path in capitals; the id never changes, a resource pack may replace the audio behind it. `event` resolves an id to the registered event, which `Level.playSound` and `Level.playLocalSound` take.

```java
level.playSound(null, player.blockPosition(), ThaumcraftSoundIds.event(ThaumcraftSoundIds.WAND),
        SoundSource.PLAYERS, 1.0F, 1.0F);   // server thread: every player in range hears it
```

```java
public static SoundEvent event(ResourceLocation id)
```

The registered sound event of an id.

**Returns:** the registered event, never `null`

**Throws:** `IllegalArgumentException` — when `id` is `null` or no sound event is registered under it (an id that does not exist, or Thaumcraft's registration has not run yet)

**Parameters:**
- `id` — one of the constants of this class, or the id of any other registered sound event

## TileThaumcraft

```java
public class TileThaumcraft extends BlockEntity
```

The original TC4 base tile entity with its own custom NBT section and a custom update packet.

Forced 1.21.1 changes: a block entity needs its registered `BlockEntityType`, the NBT hooks take a registry provider and the original `S35PacketUpdateTileEntity` became the native `ClientboundBlockEntityDataPacket`.

```java
public TileThaumcraft(BlockEntityType<?> type, BlockPos pos, BlockState state)
public void loadAdditional(CompoundTag tag, HolderLookup.Provider registries)
```


The original per-tile custom data hook.

```java
protected void saveAdditional(CompoundTag tag, HolderLookup.Provider registries)
```

<a id="tilethaumcraft-writecustomnbt"></a>
```java
public void writeCustomNBT(CompoundTag tag)
```

The original per-tile custom data hook.

<a id="tilethaumcraft-update_key"></a>
```java
public static final String UPDATE_KEY
```

The key the update tag always carries besides the custom data.

A 1.21.1 client ignores a block entity update whose tag is empty, while 1.7.10 always handed the description packet to the tile: without the key, a container whose custom data became empty (an emptied jar writes nothing) would keep its old contents on every client. `readCustomNBT` receives the key and can ignore it.

<a id="tilethaumcraft-getupdatetag"></a>
```java
public CompoundTag getUpdateTag(HolderLookup.Provider registries)
```

The custom data a client receives with the chunk and with each update.

In 1.7.10 the description packet was sent with the chunk as well as after `markBlockForUpdate`; 1.21.1 sends the chunk with this tag instead, so a client sees the custom data from the moment the block comes into view. To push a change later, call `setChanged()` and `level.sendBlockUpdated(pos, state, state, 3)`.

<a id="tilethaumcraft-getupdatepacket"></a>
```java
public Packet<ClientGamePacketListener> getUpdatePacket()
```

The original custom update packet: the custom data, read on the client by `readCustomNBT`.

## WorldCoordinates

```java
public final class WorldCoordinates implements Comparable<WorldCoordinates>
```

Immutable modern location. A dimension key is not a world lifetime: VisNet additionally scopes every graph/cache by the exact ServerLevel identity.

```java
public final int z
```
